name: agent-quickpick
description: Quick-pick launcher for agent CLI terminals — Claude, Opencode, Claude Proxy, Claude GLM, oh-my-pi, Droid, Command Code, and your own — opened in the editor area with their own icon and tab color.

agent-quickpick.description: Agent Quickpick status-bar glyph (2x2 agent grid)

agentQuickpick.agents.markdownDescription:
Custom agents shown in the quick pick. Each entry: `{name, cmd, launcher, icon, color, hidden}`. Built-ins are included automatically; to hide a built-in, repeat its `name` here with `"hidden": true`.

- **name** *(required)*: Display name (shown in quick pick + terminal tab).
- **cmd**: Shell command to launch. Empty = plain terminal. Shell functions/aliases work since VS Code terminals are interactive.
- **launcher**: Optional prefix binary (e.g. `uvx`, `npx`, `pipx`). When set, detection probes this binary on PATH and the terminal launches `${launcher} ${cmd}`.
- **icon**: A built-in codicon id (`terminal`, `rocket`, `beaker`, `hubot`, …), an absolute path to an SVG/PNG on disk, or a filename bundled with the extension (`claude.svg`). Defaults to `terminal`.
- **color**: A tab color — either an existing built-in color id (`agentQuickpick.claude`, `agentQuickpick.opencode`, …) or a stock `terminal.ansi*` key (`terminal.ansiBlue`, `terminal.ansiMagenta`, …). Optional.
- **hidden**: `true` to hide this agent.

cmd.description: Shell command to launch. Empty = plain terminal. Shell functions/aliases work.

launcher.description: Optional prefix binary (e.g. 'uvx', 'npx', 'pipx'). When set, install detection checks this binary on PATH and the terminal launches `${launcher} ${cmd}`. Useful when an agent is only runnable via a package manager.

icon.description: Codicon id (e.g. 'rocket'), absolute path to an SVG/PNG, or a bundled filename (e.g. 'claude.svg'). Default 'terminal'.

color.description: Built-in color id (agentQuickpick.claude, ...) or stock terminal.ansi* key. Optional.

hidden.description: Hide this agent from the quick pick. Use to suppress a built-in.

agentQuickpick.detectInstalled.markdownDescription: Detect installed CLIs on your PATH and warn before opening an agent whose `cmd` isn't found. Disable if your agents rely on shell aliases/functions you don't want flagged.

agentQuickpick.launchDelayMs.markdownDescription: Milliseconds to wait after opening a terminal before sending the agent's launch command. Lets other extensions (e.g. the Python extension's virtualenv auto-activation) inject their startup commands first, so they land in the shell — not inside the agent's input box. Set `0` to send immediately. Increase if activation commands still leak into an agent like Claude.

agentQuickpick.showStatusBar.markdownDescription: Show an **Agent** button in the status bar that opens the quick pick. Disable to keep the status bar uncluttered and rely on the keybinding (default `Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+A` to launch; press twice within 250ms for running sessions). Rebind it to any key via the **Change Agent Quickpick Shortcut** command or VS Code's Keyboard Shortcuts editor (`Cmd/Ctrl+K Cmd/Ctrl+S`, search `agentQuickpick.open`); the double-tap gesture follows whatever key you bind.

agentQuickpick.lifecycleNotifications.markdownDescription: Show a notification when a lifecycle-aware agent (Claude Code, OpenCode, Droid) finishes a task or needs your input. Requires a **one-time global hook install** per agent (prompted automatically the first time you launch it — installed into your user-level agent config, e.g. `~/.claude/settings.json`, so it works in every repo). The hook only reports sessions launched from Agent Quickpick and no-ops elsewhere. Remove via the "Remove Lifecycle Hooks" command. Disable for silent operation.

enumDescriptions: Never show OS notifications — in-editor toasts only.
Show an OS notification only when the VS Code window is not focused.
Always show an OS notification alongside the in-editor toast.
agentQuickpick.systemNotifications.markdownDescription: Raise a **native OS notification** (macOS Notification Center, Windows toast, Linux `notify-send`) for agent lifecycle events, not just an in-editor toast. Defaults to `always`: the OS notification is the only channel that reaches you outside the editor and the only one that persists in Notification Center, while a VS Code toast is invisible when the window is behind another app or minimized — which is exactly when "the agent needs you" matters. Requires `#agentQuickpick.lifecycleNotifications#`.

agentQuickpick.notificationSound.markdownDescription: Play Agent Quickpick's notification sound when an agent finishes, needs input, or crashes. Fires for both in-editor toasts and OS notifications, so the cue is the same wherever the notification lands. Requires `#agentQuickpick.lifecycleNotifications#`.

agentQuickpick.notificationSoundPath.markdownDescription: Absolute path to a custom notification sound, replacing the bundled cue. Use **16-bit PCM WAV** — it's the only format playable on all three platforms (Windows' `Media.SoundPlayer` accepts nothing else). Leave empty for the bundled sound.
